thread:
Marta: Thinking about an "anchorless" sampler for quant calibration pools — goal is to avoid anchor bias in the calibration set while keeping small anchor probes for regression tracking. Thoughts? :thinking:
Jon: Can you clarify "anchorless"? we still keep anchors for regression windows right?
Marta: Right — separate tiny anchor probe (<=200 prompts) for monitoring. The calibration pool itself would be sampled without baked-in anchors to avoid overfitting quant config to those examples.
Sameer: Agree. Practical proposal: stratified sampling by prompt class + difficulty + length. Example allocation: 40% common intents, 30% long-context (>512 tokens), 15% code/snippet, 10% instruction-following, 5% adversarial/edgecases.
Lia: That split looks reasonable. How big is the calibration pool for initial bakeoff? 5k? 10k?
Marta: Start 5k for quick iterate, 20k for final runs. Must ensure de-dup across train/test and remove templated system prompts.
Jon: We should add negative controls and perturbations: paraphrase variants, prefix noise, swapped entities. Helps detect brittle quantization bugs.
Sameer: +1. Also include a holdout per-stratum for evaluation (10% holdout) so we can compute accuracy deltas w/o leakage.
Lia: What metrics are we tracking? exact-match, SAcc, LM perplexity, and a scalar "regression hit" when delta > threshold.
Marta: Proposed thresholds: for major policies (INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8) per-profile allowed delta < 1% absolute on primary metric, <2% on secondary. Flag auto-fail otherwise.
Sameer: For code tasks track compilation rate / run-time correctness — different tolerances.
Jon: Sampling pseudo-config I sketched for the sampler: 
```
seed: 42
strata: ["intent","length","code","adv"]
weights: [0.4,0.3,0.15,0.15]
per_strata_holdout: 0.1
max_dup_tokens: 0.8
```
We can tune weights per workload.
Marta: Implementation note: sampler should avoid heavy token overlap with model pretrain corpora (use fingerprinting) to avoid "memorized answers" inflating scores.
Lia: For deployment profiles we need separate calibration pools: hosted (low-latency short seq dist), dedicated (mixed long seq), private (customer-specific prompt shapes). Sampling weights should be adjusted per-profile.
Sameer: Bakeoff plan: run 4 quant methods (FP8, GPTQ, AWQ, INT8 baseline) across 3 profiles (hosted/dedicated/private) using the 5k anchorless calibration pool + 200-anchor probes. Generate per-profile accuracy delta table and per-stratum breakdown.
Jon: How long will runs take? GPU estimate?
Marta: Small runs on 1-2 A100s for 8-12h for 5k with batching. Larger 20k runs ~1-2d. We'll parallelize across machines.
Lia: Can eval-bot auto-ingest results and compute regression hits? If we standardize CSV format it's easy.
eval-bot: I can ingest results if they follow schema: run_id, model_variant, quant_method, profile, prompt_id, metric, score. Will post summary heatmaps. :robot_face:
Sameer: Also include a tiny "sanity anchor" of rare edgecases that we never sample into calibration pool but use only for long-term regression tracking. Keep it immutable.
Marta: Decision draft: implement anchorless sampler for calibration pools with stratified weights, keep a separate tiny anchor guardrail probe + immutable sanity anchor set, run 5k initial bakeoff across FP8/GPTQ/AWQ/INT8, measure per-profile deltas. If pass thresholds, scale to 20k.
Jon: :thumbsup: I'll open a PR with the sampler spec and a script to produce the 5k splits.
Lia: I'll own the anchor probe and the sanity anchor list (curation + dedupe).
Sameer: I'll wire the bakeoff runner and the eval dashboards.
Marta: Thanks everyone. We'll sync next week with initial numbers.
Jon: Quick question — random seed reproducibility and run configs should be checked into repo. Also include a small README about sampling invariants.
Marta: Agreed. Tagging @lia @sameer for follow-ups.
Lia: noted.
Marta: End.
